Description: A short descriptive name for this analytical procedure, including a version number. Should identify the instrument, the technique, and the scope of what is measured — analyte, material, or feature.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'LA-ICP-MS Trace Elements Silicate Glass v1.2' | 'fs-LA-ICP-MS Major and Trace Elements Sulfide v1'

Description: Top-level analytical technique identifier.
Example / Allowed Content: LA-MC-ICP-MS

Description: Person(s) or laboratory responsible for developing and registering this procedure. ORCID recommended for individuals.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'J. Smith (ORCID: 0000-0001-2345-6789)' | 'Isotope Geochemistry Lab, University of X'

Description: Name of the laboratory or institution hosting the instrument.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Geo-/Cosmochemistry Lab, University of Cologne'

Description: Persistent identifier for the laboratory (e.g., ROR ID).
Example / Allowed Content: ROR ID or equivalent URI (https://ror.org/)

Description: First date this procedure configuration was used in production.

Grants and other funding sources that supported instrument acquisition, major upgrades, procedure development, and associated personnel time. Include grant numbers and funding agencies where applicable.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'NSF EAR-2142500; DFG INST 216/1019-1 FUGG no. 665508' | 'None'

Description: DOI or URL for peer-reviewed publications or technical reports describing, validating, or benchmarking this procedure.

DOI or unique persistent identifier for the registered procedure used in this analysis, generated upon procedure submission to a data repository. If a DOI has been applied for but not yet minted, enter "pending".
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., http://doi.org/10.60520/IEDA/114187 | pending
Purpose: Encourages formal procedure registration and ensures traceability.

Description: Identifier for the analytical session this record describes — the laboratory's own run, sequence or batch identifier as generated by the instrument or acquisition software. Distinct from any persistent identifier a repository mints on submission.
Purpose: The analysis record corresponds to one session, which may cover several samples, and this is the link back to the raw instrument files.

Description: Name(s) of the analyst(s) who performed the analysis session. ORCID is recommended for persistent identification.
Date on which the analytical session began. For sessions spanning multiple days, use the date of the first session. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.
Date on which the analytical session ended. May equal Analysis Start Date for single-day sessions. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

Grants and other funding sources that supported the specific sample analyses and data collection reported here. Include grant numbers and funding agencies. Distinct from procedure development funding, which may have been awarded years earlier.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'NASA 80NSSC21K0153; DFG WE 2850/5-1' | 'None'

Description: Other analytical techniques applied to the same sample(s) whose results are intended to be interpreted together with data from this procedure. Document coupling with any technique whose results are functionally linked to this dataset — providing calibration inputs, complementary spatial context, or required companion measurements. Name the instrument, laboratory or purpose alongside each technique where known, and join multiple techniques with '; '. Enter "None" if no coupling is intended.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'EPMA (Brown University CAMECA SX-100)' | 'FIB-SEM (Crossbeam 540) for 3D tomography; EDS for mineral analysis' | 'NanoSIMS; STXM; Raman' | 'None' | 'N/A'

Description: Description of how this procedure is coupled with the technique(s) listed above. Include: (1) the functional relationship — what data or context flows between techniques, or how results are combined (e.g. which output from the coupled technique serves as input to data reduction for this technique); and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique is performed first and why (e.g. non-destructive before destructive). Required when Coupled Technique(s) is not "None".
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'EPMA provides major element concentrations (SiO₂ as internal standard) used in LA-ICP-MS data reduction; EPMA performed first because LA-ICP-MS ablation is destructive' | 'SIMS isotope ratios cross-validated against LA-ICP-MS; SIMS performed first due to shallower beam penetration'

Description: Registered procedure DOI for the coupled technique named above. If the coupled procedure has not yet been registered, enter the DOI of a publication describing the coupled method, or "pending". Enter "None" if no coupling is planned.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'http://doi.org/10.60520/IEDA/114187' | pending | None
Purpose: Provides a stable, citable link to the companion method independent of whether a dataset has been deposited.

Description: DOI or other persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication where both datasets are reported together. Accepts: a dedicated dataset DOI (if separately deposited), a shared dataset DOI (if co-submitted in the same package), or a publication DOI. Use "same submission" if the coupled dataset is included in this data package, or "pending" if not yet assigned. If coupling is documented through a shared sample identifier only, that information is already captured in Sample Persistent Identifier (Group 2).
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'doi:10.26022/IEDA/112969' | same submission | pending | None

Description: General description of the material type(s) this procedure is designed to analyse.
Example / Allowed Content: Silicate glass | Feldspar | Pyroxene | Olivine | Oxide | Sulfide | Carbonate | Phosphate | Native metal | Iron meteorite | Fluid inclusion | Melt inclusion | Whole rock | N/A | None
Purpose: Used for discoverability and procedure matching, and because the material type constrains sample preparation, calibration and matrix-matching requirements.

Description: Physical form of the material as it enters the ablation cell. Variations that do not alter the analytical procedure (e.g., thin section vs. mount) are legitimate.
Example / Allowed Content: In situ — polished thin section | In situ — polished epoxy mount | In situ — polished thick section | Pressed powder pellet | Li-borate fused glass disc | Nano-particulate pressed pellet | Liquid | N/A | None

Description: Name or identifier of each sample analysed in this session, as used in the laboratory — a sample mount, section or aliquot counts as one entry where that is what the laboratory tracks. Should match the identifier used in associated publications or data tables.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'NWA 10597 ol-1' | 'Imilac PMG section 3 grain 2'
Purpose: The analysis record corresponds to one session and may cover several samples.

Description: The physical subdivision of the sample to which one row of reported values corresponds — the unit that is analysed and reported, as distinct from the sample as a whole. Where units nest (e.g. confined tracks within grains), state both levels.
Example / Allowed Content: Whole sample | Aliquot | Grain | Spot | Analysis point | Phase | Sub-volume | Region of interest | N/A | None

Description: Globally unique, persistent identifier for each sample listed in Sample Name. IGSN (International Geo Sample Number) is the recommended standard for geological and cosmochemical samples, as used by Astromat, EarthChem and SESAR. Where a sample and its sub-samples are separately registered, record the identifier at the level actually analysed.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., IGSN: IEDA-100001 (https://www.igsn.org/) | Smithsonian NMNH catalog number

Description: For procedures using fused glass, the flux type and sample:flux dilution ratio used to prepare the analytical glass.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Li-tetraborate, 1:2 (sample:flux)' | 'Li-metaborate/tetraborate 50:50, 1:5' | 'Not applicable (in situ)'

Description: The form in which the sample is presented to the instrument, and the preparation that brought it to that form — for example mounting, sectioning, polishing, coating, crushing, fusion, or extraction of an electron-transparent section. Record 'None' where the material is analysed as received.
Example / Allowed Content: Polished thin section | Polished thick section | Polished block or epoxy mount | Grain mount | Fused bead | Experimental capsule section | Etched or chemically treated surface | N/A | None

Description: Procedure applied immediately before each analysis to remove surface contamination or condition the sample surface. Distinct from general sample preparation. For spot analysis, pre-ablation pulses are discarded before signal acquisition begins. For mapping, this step is typically omitted.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '10 pre-ablation pulses discarded before acquisition (50 µm, 10 Hz, 2 J cm⁻²)' | '150 µm square spot, 2 J cm⁻², 20 Hz, 300 µm s⁻¹ pre-ablation pass (Chernonozhkin et al. 2021)' | 'None'
Purpose: In mapping the large area ablated averages out surface effects.

Description: The rules governing which part of the sample is analysed, and why. Covers the criteria applied when choosing grains, aliquots, spots, or a region of interest — size, morphology, clarity, freedom from inclusions or alteration, phase identity, or spatial position. Distinct from Target Material, which states the material type the procedure is designed for: this field states how, within such a sample, the analysed portion is picked out.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Euhedral, crack- and inclusion-free grains 80-150 um; oscillatory-zoned rims targeted, inherited cores avoided on CL' | 'All grains in the separate analysed (detrital provenance)'

Description: Imaging or other characterisation performed before the measurement in order to select or locate the analysed target, including the technique, instrument and settings used, and how individual analyses are linked back to the images. Distinct from any imaging the procedure performs as its own measurement. Where the imaging is performed on a separate instrument, it should also be recorded in the Group 1 coupling fields.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'CL imaging on Zeiss Sigma SEM at 10 kV before spot placement; every dated grain imaged and spot positions annotated' | 'BSE and CL mosaics; micro-Raman screening of chemical-abrasion effectiveness (McKanna et al. 2023)'

Description: Annealing and partial-dissolution conditions applied to mitigate Pb loss before analysis, following Mattinson (2005): annealing temperature and duration, and the acid, temperature and duration of the partial-dissolution step. Record 'None' where grains were analysed untreated.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Annealed 900 C, 60 h; partial dissolution 12 M HF, 210 C, 12 h' | 'Annealed 850 C, 48 h; 29 M HF, 180 C, 12 h' | 'None (untreated)'
Purpose: Condon et al. (2024) require these where chemical abrasion was applied, and state that it generally should be for zircon. The absence of treatment materially affects how discordance should be read.

Description: Manufacturer and model of the laser ablation system.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'ESI/NWR imageGEO193' | 'Coherent GeoLas HD' | 'Teledyne Analyte Excite 193' | 'Teledyne Analyte G2'

Description: Manufacturer of the instrument that performs the measurement, recorded as a controlled value. Where a procedure couples a sample-introduction system to an analysing instrument, this records the analysing instrument. Instrument Model gives the specific designation.
Example / Allowed Content: Thermo Fisher Scientific | Agilent | PerkinElmer | Nu Instruments | Analytik Jena | Shimadzu | Unknown | N/A | None
Purpose: Recording it as a controlled value lets procedures be found by vendor.

Description: Model designation of the instrument that performs the measurement, including any generation or configuration suffix. Conventionally written with the manufacturer name included; Instrument Manufacturer records the vendor separately, as a controlled value, so that procedures remain findable by vendor.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Thermo Scientific iCAP TQ' | 'Agilent 7900' | 'Thermo Scientific Element XR' | 'TOFWERK icpTOF'

Description: Type of ICP-MS system - the mass analyser and, where the instrument has one, the collector configuration.
Example / Allowed Content: Multi-collector (MC-ICP-MS) | Multi-collector with collision/reaction cell (e.g. Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS) | N/A | None
Purpose: Determines available cell configurations and interference mitigation strategies.

Metadata Item: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier
Description: Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Element XR S/N 1234' | 'Lab unit: Ghent-SF2'
Purpose: Supports traceability to instrument service records.

Description: Geometry and designation of the sampler and skimmer cones installed during analysis. State both cones.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Ni standard sample cone + Ni H-type skimmer' | 'Al standard sample cone + Al H-type skimmer (1.1 mm aperture)' | 'Pt sample cone + Pt skimmer'
Purpose: Some instruments offer multiple skimmer cone geometries (standard, high-sensitivity) that differ in aperture size and affect ion transmission efficiency and matrix tolerance.

Description: Material composition of the sampler and skimmer cones. State both sampler and skimmer materials; a single statement is acceptable where they are identical.
Example / Allowed Content: Nickel (Ni) sampler and skimmer cones (standard configuration); Platinum (Pt) sampler, nickel (Ni) skimmer
Purpose: Cone material affects sensitivity, matrix tolerance, and long-term stability.

Description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position depending on the instrument manufacturer.
Example / Allowed Content: 5 mm; Standard position (manufacturer default; not explicitly reported)
Purpose: Affects ion transmission efficiency, oxide formation, and doubly-charged species production.

Description: Type of plasma torch installed (e.g. standard quartz, high-matrix, low-flow).
Example / Allowed Content: Standard quartz | High-matrix (low-flow) | Low-volume | N/A | None
Purpose: Injector inner diameter (typically 1.5–2.5 mm) affects aerosol transport efficiency and plasma conditions in LA-ICP-MS.

Description: Whether a guard electrode - also called a grounded shield electrode, extraction lens, or Fassel torch shield - is installed and active on the torch assembly.
Example / Allowed Content: On | Off | Not installed | N/A | None
Purpose: Capacitively decouples the plasma from the load coil, reducing secondary discharge and improving ion extraction efficiency.

Description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. Where the analyser permits selection, state the mode; where individual analytes are assigned to different modes, state each.
Example / Allowed Content: Unit resolution (quadrupole, fixed) | Low resolution (LR) | Medium resolution (MR) | High resolution (HR) | Multiple modes assigned per analyte | N/A | None
Purpose: For quadrupole instruments this is fixed at unit resolution by instrument design. For sector-field instruments the analyst selects low, medium, or high resolution to balance sensitivity against spectral interference suppression.

Description: Type(s) of detector(s) installed in the mass spectrometer. For single-collector instruments, note whether dual pulse-counting/analog mode is used. For multi-collector instruments, describe the Faraday/multiplier cup layout.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Single SEM, dual mode (pulse counting and analog)' | 'Single SEM in triple mode (pulse, analog, Faraday)' | 'Nine Faraday cups + one ion counter (MC)'

Description: Whether a collision or reaction cell is installed and its operating mode. In standard mode (STD), no cell gas is introduced and the cell acts only as an ion guide. In kinetic energy discrimination (KED) mode, helium thermalizes ions so that polyatomic interferences, which have a larger collision cross-section, are selectively retarded by a cell exit barrier voltage. In dynamic reaction cell (DRC) mode, a reactive gas selectively neutralizes specific interferences through ion-molecule reactions. Specific gas types, flow rates and cell voltages are documented in Group 4. Record 'Not installed' where the instrument has no collision/reaction cell.
Example / Allowed Content: Not installed | STD (standard mode, no gas) | KED (kinetic energy discrimination, He gas) | DRC (dynamic reaction cell, reactive gas) | KED+DRC | MS/MS (pre-cell mass filter) | N/A | None
Purpose: On MS/MS instruments a second mass filter preceding the cell enables precursor-ion selection.

Description: Wavelength and type of the laser used for ablation in nanometres.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '193 nm ArF excimer' | '213 nm Nd:YAG frequency-quintupled' | '257 nm Yb:KGW femtosecond' | '1030 nm Yb:KGW IR femtosecond'

Description: Instrument control, automation and data acquisition software used to collect the raw data, including version number. Distinct from Data Processing Software(s), which covers everything applied to the data after acquisition.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Thermo Qtegra 2.10.3324' | 'Agilent MassHunter Workstation 4.6' | 'Thermo PlasmaLab 2.5.4'

Description: All software applied to the data after acquisition in order to produce the reported quantities, including version numbers. List every package used. Distinct from Acquisition Software, which controls the instrument and collects the raw data.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Iolite 4.7 (Paton et al. 2011)' | 'GLITTER 4.4' | 'SILLS 1.1.5 (Guillong et al. 2008)' | 'LAtools' | 'In-house MatLab script'

Description: Type, design origin, and internal volume of the ablation cell.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Two-volume HelEx II (Müller et al. 2009)' | 'HDIP low-dispersion tube-type cell' | 'Single-volume standard cell' | 'ARIS (Aerosol Rapid Introduction System)'
Purpose: Cell volume is a primary determinant of aerosol washout time and therefore the achievable time resolution of the data.

Description: Configuration by which the ablated aerosol is delivered to the plasma, including tubing, any signal-homogenising device, and any co-aspirated solution introduced alongside the aerosol — for example a Tl solution used for instrumental mass bias correction, or an isotopic spike used for isotope dilution. Distinct from the carrier and make-up gas fields, which record gas identity and flow rather than what else enters the plasma.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Squid signal homogeniser, 2 m PTFE tubing, no co-aspiration' | 'Dry plasma; Tl solution co-aspirated via desolvating nebuliser for mass bias correction'

Description: Description of the multi-collector Faraday cup array. Specify the total number of Faraday cup detectors (fixed and moveable), their labeled positions (e.g., L4, L3, L2, L1, Ax, H1, H2, H3, H4 for a 9-cup Neptune), and the presence and position of any ion counter (SEM) or Daly detector in the collector block.
Purpose: The number and span of cups constrains which isotope combinations can be simultaneously collected.

Description: Resistance values (Ω) of the feedback resistors in the Faraday cup amplifiers. Standard amplifiers use 10¹¹ Ω resistors, yielding 1 V per ~6.24 × 10⁶ ion counts per second. Report the resistor value per cup position, or note 'all 10¹¹ Ω' if uniform.
Purpose: High-gain amplifiers (10¹² or 10¹³ Ω) are fitted to selected cups to improve signal-to-noise for very low-intensity beams (e.g., 234U, low-abundance spike isotopes).

Description: Method used to calibrate the relative gain (amplification factor) of each Faraday cup amplifier at the start of or during each analytical session. Common approaches: instrument internal gain calibration routine (measures signal in each cup sequentially using a common beam), amplifier rotation procedure, or measurement of a known isotope ratio solution in each cup. For instruments with SEM detectors, also describes the SEM-to-Faraday cross-calibration sequence. Specify frequency (per session, per block, weekly).
Purpose: Relative gain differences between amplifiers cause systematic errors in isotope ratios if uncorrected.

Description: Primary analytical mode(s) executed under this procedure. Records one value for a single-mode procedure and all applicable modes for a multi-mode one. Applies even where a procedure defines no mode flag columns.
Example / Allowed Content: 'Spot' | 'Transect' | 'Mapping' | 'Spot; Transect' | 'Spot; Mapping'
Purpose: Serves as the procedure-level declaration of measurement type, distinct from the mode flag columns, which state per-field applicability. Ensures every procedure record is self-describing and comparable across the library.

Description: Shape and dimensions of the laser ablation spot in micrometres registered by the procedure. For circular spots, report diameter; for square or rectangular spots, report width × length.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '25 µm circular' | '20×20 µm square' | '15 or 25 µm circular (phase-dependent)'

Description: Diameter of the laser spot as independently measured on the sample or on a test material, distinct from the nominal value the procedure registers.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '32.4' | 'nominal 35, measured 33.1 +/- 0.8 (n = 12 pits, white-light profilometry)'
Purpose: Measured companion to Laser Spot Geometry: nominal and delivered spot size can differ appreciably with optics condition and focus.

Description: Sampling mode or ablation pattern used during analysis.
Example / Allowed Content: Spot (stationary) | Transect (continuous line scan) | Raster area (2D elemental mapping) | Stepped line profile | N/A | None

Description: Laser pulse energy in millijoules as set at the laser output or measured at the sample surface. Report only when the system displays energy directly. Laser fluence (J cm⁻²) is the preferred quantity and is captured in Laser Fluence (Energy Density).
Purpose: Less commonly reported than fluence because it does not account for spot area.

Description: Laser pulse energy per unit area at the sample surface in J cm⁻², as registered by the procedure. If the system reports only as % of maximum output, include that value and note the system maximum where known.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '3.5 J cm⁻²' | '7 J cm⁻²' | '60% output (PHAROS system, max ~15 J cm⁻²)'
Purpose: Fluence is the physically meaningful quantity controlling ablation rate, crater morphology, elemental fractionation, and particle size distribution.

Description: Spatial energy distribution of the laser beam at the sample surface, and whether a beam homogenizer is installed.
Example / Allowed Content: Flat-top (top-hat) — beam homogenizer installed | Gaussian — no beam homogenizer | N/A | None
Purpose: A flat-top (top-hat) profile produces more uniform ablation craters and more reproducible crater morphology than a Gaussian beam.

Description: Laser pulse repetition rate in hertz registered by the procedure.
Purpose: For mapping methods, repetition rate together with scan speed and spot size determines pixel size and spatial resolution.

Description: Duration of each individual laser pulse, including units.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '4 ns (ArF excimer)' | '20 ns' | '290 fs (Yb:KGW)' | '220 fs (Ti:sapphire)'
Purpose: Pulse duration determines the ablation regime: nanosecond (ns) pulses involve significant thermal effects and elemental fractionation; femtosecond (fs) pulses are non-thermal and substantially reduce elemental fractionation and matrix effects.

Description: Total on-sample ablation (signal acquisition) time per individual spot in seconds, as set in the acquisition method. For transect analysis, the equivalent procedure-level parameter is scan speed (captured in Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size). For mapping analysis, total acquisition time is sample-area-dependent and is not captured here.
Purpose: For spot analysis, reflects the deliberate trade-off between signal accumulation (longer = lower LOD), sample consumption, and session throughput.

Metadata Item: Ablation Pit Depth and Ablation Rate
Description: Depth of the ablation pit produced under the registered laser conditions, the method used to measure it, and the resulting per-pulse ablation rate. For transect and mapping the equivalent quantity is trench depth under the same conditions.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Pit depth 18 um after 300 pulses (white-light profilometry); 60 nm/pulse' | 'Trench depth 4 um at 5 um/s scan speed'
Purpose: Sets the achievable depth resolution and governs downhole elemental fractionation.

Metadata Item: Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size
Description: For continuous line scan (transect) and raster mapping: the stage translation speed in µm s⁻¹. For mapping, the mapping rate (mm² h⁻¹) may be reported as an alternative when scan speed is session-variable. For stepped line profiles: the distance between successive spot positions in µm.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '5 µm s⁻¹ (transect)' | '9 µm s⁻¹ (raster mapping, 20×20 µm spot, 20 Hz)' | '20 µm step size' | '0.3–30 mm² h⁻¹ (mapping rate range)'
Purpose: Together with spot size and repetition rate, determines spatial resolution along the scan direction.

Description: Distance between adjacent raster lines in a 2D elemental map, measured perpendicular to the scan direction, in micrometres. Applies to raster mapping only.
Example / Allowed Content: 20 µm (contiguous, equal to spot size) | 15 µm pitch with 5 µm gap between lines | N/A (spot or line-scan mode)
Purpose: Together with spot size, this determines whether adjacent lines are contiguous (line spacing = spot size), overlapping (line spacing < spot size), or have gaps (line spacing > spot size).

Description: Gas used to transport ablated aerosol from the ablation cell to the ICP-MS torch, with the procedure-registered target flow rate(s). Adjustment during tuning stays within ±10% of the target.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'He, 0.75 l min⁻¹' | 'He: MFC-1 (cell) 0.60 l min⁻¹ + MFC-2 (cup) 0.35 l min⁻¹'
Purpose: Helium is standard for most UV laser systems due to superior aerosol transport.

Description: Supplementary gas added to the sample-carrying stream between the sample introduction system and the plasma, with its identity and the procedure-registered target flow rate. Record any small nitrogen or hydrogen addition with its own flow, whose unit commonly differs from the make-up flow. Record 'None' explicitly where no supplementary gas is added, to distinguish it from not reported.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Ar make-up gas, 0.95 l min⁻¹' | 'Ar make-up 0.80 l min⁻¹ + N₂ 2 ml min⁻¹ (sensitivity enhancement)' | 'None (no N₂ added)'
Purpose: Argon make-up is standard and maintains total gas delivery where the carrier flow alone is insufficient — downstream of an ablation cell, or of a desolvation system that has removed solvent load. Small nitrogen or hydrogen additions enhance sensitivity for some elements.

Description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma, in L/min.
Example / Allowed Content: 14 L/min | 15 L/min
Purpose: Determines plasma volume and stability.

Description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream, between the torch body and the injector tube, which positions the plasma relative to the load coil, in L/min. Distinct from the outer coolant (plasma) gas and from the gas stream that carries sample into the plasma.
Example / Allowed Content: 0.8 L/min | 1.0 L/min | 1.2 L/min
Purpose: Affects ion extraction efficiency and oxide production rates.

Description: Radiofrequency forward power applied to the ICP, in watts.
Purpose: Affects plasma temperature, ionisation efficiency, oxide formation, and whether cool or normal plasma conditions are in effect.

Description: Whether the ICP plasma is operated under cool plasma (<=900 W RF) or normal (hot) plasma (>1000 W RF) conditions, with the RF power that defines it. This field records the RF-POWER axis only. Solvent loading also affects plasma thermal state, but dry versus wet aerosol is recorded by Desolvation System — do not answer this field with 'dry plasma' or 'wet plasma'. Document independently of the RF Power field.
Example / Allowed Content: Normal plasma (>1000 W RF) | Cool plasma (≤900 W RF) | Mixed: specify mode per analytical sub-run | N/A | None
Purpose: Cool plasma substantially reduces argide-based polyatomic interferences (e.g., ⁴⁰Ar on ⁴⁰Ca, ⁴⁰Ar⁴⁰Ar on ⁸⁰Se). A fundamental method design choice that determines which interference corrections are necessary.

Description: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability. For mapping analyses, report "None" explicitly.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Squid 2.0 (laurin technik)' | 'ARIS (Aerosol Rapid Introduction System)' | 'None'
Purpose: Note: active signal smoothing devices (e.g., squid, SCFAST) are generally incompatible with high-resolution raster mapping because they degrade spatial resolution by mixing aerosol from successive laser shots.

Description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Daily auto-tune on NIST SRM 612; optimised for max sensitivity on ¹³⁹La and ²³²Th with ThO⁺/Th⁺ <0.5% and U/Th = 1.0 ± 0.05'

Description: Instrument sensitivity achieved in the session, with the isotope or channel it was measured on and the conditions it applies to. May be expressed either as detected signal per unit concentration or per unit mass of analyte delivered — counts per second per ppb, volts per ppm, counts per picogram — or as useful yield, the percentage of sampled atoms ultimately detected as ions, with the method used to derive it cited. A sensitivity the procedure requires before analyses may begin belongs with the tuning acceptance criteria.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '0.42% useful yield (U, method of Horstwood et al. 2016)' | '0.1% useful yield (analytes, msfs-LA-ICP-MS)' | '1.2 x 10^6 cps/ppb on 115In' | 'N/A'
Purpose: Useful yield is the more comparable of the two wherever the amount of material consumed varies between procedures, as it does with spot size, fluence and repetition rate.

Description: Method used to quantify plasma oxide production and the acceptance threshold applied before commencing analysis. Record both the monitored mass ratio(s) and the maximum allowed threshold(s). Measured values are recorded in Oxide Production. The monitored ratio is procedure-dependent: ThO+/Th+ (m/z 248/232), UO+/U+ (254/238), CeO+/Ce+ (156/140) and BaO+/Ba+ are all in use.

Measured oxide production ratio obtained during session-start tuning, for the proxy specified in Oxide Production Method and Threshold. Record the measured value and confirm whether the procedure threshold was met.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'ThO⁺/Th⁺ = 0.3% (threshold <0.5% met)' | 'ThO⁺/Th⁺ = 0.08%' | 'CeO⁺/Ce⁺ = 0.7% (threshold <1.0% met)'

Description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning. The monitor species and the mass positions monitored should be stated explicitly. Analogous to Oxide Production Method and Threshold for oxide monitoring.
Example / Allowed Content: ¹³⁸Ba²⁺/¹³⁸Ba⁺ (m/z 69/138); Ce²⁺/Ce⁺ (m/z 70/140); ²³⁸U²⁺/²³⁸U⁺ (m/z 119/238)
Purpose: Doubly-charged ions appear at half the mass of the parent ion and can cause isobaric interferences on analytes in that mass region.

Description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning. The acceptable threshold is typically <1% or <3%. Record both the threshold and the measured value.
Example / Allowed Content: <1% (threshold); 0.4% (measured, ¹³⁸Ba²⁺/¹³⁸Ba⁺); N (not reported)

Description: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '≥30 min warm-up after sample change; sessions ≤8 h after tuning' | '3–4 h warm-up; no session duration limit'

Description: The repeating order in which calibration or bracketing standards, quality-control and secondary reference materials, blanks and unknowns are interleaved within a measurement session. Adjustments must maintain the bracketing strategy defined in the procedure.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '1 primary std / 1 QC / 10 unknowns' | '2/4/15' | 'Calibration at start and end; unknowns in between'

Description: The chemical species this procedure is designed to determine, recorded at whatever resolution the chemistry is resolved — element(s) for this technique; valence species where a procedure resolves oxidation state; compounds where it resolves molecules. Isotopes are not analytes: isotopes of an element are the same chemical species. The subset actually measured may be narrower than the registered suite where species were excluded due to interferences or scope reduction.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Major elements: Mg, Si, Ca, Fe; Trace elements: Sc, V, Cr ... U' | 'All REE: La-Lu'

Description: Specific masses monitored in this procedure, grouped by the analyte element they serve where they serve one. Covers atomic isotopes and, where a reaction cell shifts an analyte onto a different mass, the product mass actually measured. Includes interference-monitor and internal-standard masses, which serve no analyte and so have no parent element. The analyte list is given by the Analyte field and is never inferred from the element symbols appearing here.
Example / Allowed Content: ⁷Li | ²⁵Mg | ⁵⁶Fe | ²⁰⁸Pb | N/A | None

Description: The final variable(s) this procedure reports and their units — distinct from the fields recording what was *acquired* rather than what is reported. Record every reported variable, including intermediate quantities reported alongside final ones (e.g. both the 206Pb/238U ratio and the 206Pb/238U date). Where a reported variable is a nominal property with no magnitude (e.g. a mineral identification), record the variable and give the unit as 'N/A — nominal property'.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Element concentrations in ug/g; 2SE per analyte' | '207Pb/206Pb, 206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U (radiogenic, common-Pb corrected), absolute ratios with 2-sigma'
Purpose: A procedure may acquire many channels and report a small number of derived quantities; without this field a data consumer cannot tell which.

Description: Mass resolution mode used for acquisition. One analyte may be acquired at more than one resolution, so the assignment is per acquired mass rather than per element. The overall mode(s) used in the procedure are recorded in Mass Resolution Setting (Group 3).
Example / Allowed Content: LR: Ag, Cd, Sb, Tl, Bi; MR: Ga, Ge, Mo, In, Sn, W | All LR (m/Δm ≈ 300) | N/A | None
Purpose: The selected resolution determines which polyatomic interferences are physically resolved by the magnetic sector.

Description: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in the dead-time correction applied to high count rates. Distinct from pulse/analog cross-calibration, which relates the two detector modes rather than correcting counting losses within the pulse-counting mode.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '23' | '23 ns (determined from NIST 612 at varying spot size, checked quarterly)'

Description: Type of collision gas introduced into the collision/reaction cell for PHYSICAL energy discrimination (KED), where an inert gas thermalizes ions and polyatomic interferences are retarded by their larger collision cross-section. Typically He. Record a gas here when it is used without intended chemistry; where the same gas is also used to drive a mass shift, record that use under Reaction Gas Type — O2 is attested in both roles. Record 'None' if the cell is in STD mode, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include KED or the instrument has no cell.
Example / Allowed Content: He | H2 | He+H2 | O2 | N/A | None
Purpose: Helium (He) is the standard collision gas for kinetic energy discrimination, being low in mass and chemically inert.

Description: Flow rate of the collision gas, typically He, introduced into the collision/reaction cell in KED mode, in mL/min. Record 'None' if the cell is in STD mode, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include KED or the instrument has no cell.
Example / Allowed Content: 3.5 mL/min | 4.0 mL/min | None (STD mode) | N/A
Purpose: Controls the degree of ion thermalization and KED efficiency; higher flow rates give greater interference suppression at the cost of analyte sensitivity.

Description: Bias voltage applied at the collision/reaction cell exit to discriminate between analyte ions and low-energy polyatomic interferences in KED mode, in volts (V). Record 'None' if the cell is in STD mode, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include KED or the instrument has no cell.
Example / Allowed Content: −5 V | −8 V | None (STD mode) | N/A
Purpose: A negative bias preferentially retards slow polyatomic ions while transmitting faster analyte ions, controlling the degree of polyatomic suppression.

Description: Type of reactive gas introduced into the cell for interference removal through ION-MOLECULE CHEMISTRY, either on-mass or by mass shift. Common reaction gases include NH₃ (e.g., for Fe, Ca, K isotopes), O₂ (e.g., for As, Ge, Te mass shift) and CH₄. The distinction from Collision Gas Type is the mechanism, not the gas: record a gas here when a reaction is intended. Record 'None' if no reactive gas is used, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include a reaction mode or the instrument has no cell.
Example / Allowed Content: NH3 | O2 | CH4 | N/A | None

Description: Flow rate of the reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC), in mL/min. Record 'None' if DRC mode is not used, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include DRC or the instrument has no cell.
Example / Allowed Content: 0.4 mL/min | 0.8 mL/min | None | N/A

Description: Total time spent measuring gas blank (background signal with laser off or shutter closed) before each ablation event, in seconds. For spot and transect analysis, a discrete background interval is measured before each ablation. For mapping, background is typically measured once per raster line or at the start of a map session rather than before each individual pixel.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '30 s (spot/transect)' | '10 s per raster line (mapping)' | '25 s (one gas blank map per GRM at session start)'

Description: Whether the procedure uses a single acquisition pass or multiple sequential runs on the same sample location, each optimized for different analytical objectives. For multi-run designs, describe the number of runs, their purpose, key laser and instrument settings per run, and how outputs of one run feed into data reduction of another. Not applicable to raster mapping, where each spatial location is visited exactly once.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., Single run | Two sequential runs: run 1 (major elements, 30 µm circular, medium resolution) → run 2 (trace elements, 130 µm circular, low resolution; Cr from run 1 as IS) | Pre-ablation pass + single acquisition run

Description: Location of the analysis on the sample surface. For spot and transect analysis: stage coordinates (X, Y in µm) or a description relative to a named reference feature (e.g., mineral rim, inclusion boundary). For mapping: coordinates of the map corner(s) or centre, plus map dimensions.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'X = 12350 µm, Y = 8760 µm (stage coordinates)' | '500 µm from metal-olivine rim toward core' | 'Map centre: X=15000, Y=9000 µm; area: 1450×600 µm'
Purpose: Enables spatial reconstruction and co-registration with other analytical images.

Description: Number of replicate measurements performed on the same sample, or on the same nominal location where the technique is spatially resolved. For spot analysis this is the number of individual spots per grain or location; for transects, the number of replicate lines; for mapping, the number of map acquisitions of the same area; for solution work, the number of discrete replicate measurements acquired per sample solution.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 3 (three replicate spots per grain) | 1 (single transect) | 1 (single map)

Description: Total length of the transect line analysed in micrometres. Scan speed is captured separately in Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size.
Purpose: Depends on the size of the feature of interest rather than being fixed in the procedure.

Description: Total area covered by the 2D raster map, expressed as width × height in µm or as total area in µm² or mm². Scan speed, line spacing and spot size are fixed by the procedure; the map area covers the target feature.
Purpose: The map area depends on the size of the grain or phase to be mapped.

Description: Assignment of isotope masses to Faraday cup or ion counter detector positions for this procedure, and the analyte each position serves. Lists the mass number monitored in each collector position with its analyte element where it has one — e.g. 'L3=116Sn (Sn); L2=117Sn (Sn); Ax=120Sn (Sn); H1=121Sb (interference monitor, no analyte)'. Interference-monitor and internal-standard positions serve no analyte and carry no parent element; the analyte list itself is given by the Analyte field and is never inferred from the mass labels here. For static multi-collection procedures, one configuration applies throughout the measurement. For multi-dynamic procedures, list all configurations and the cycling sequence.
Purpose: Different element systems require different mass assignments within the collector array span.

Description: Number of measurement blocks acquired per sample or standard solution introduction. In MC-ICP-MS, data are structured as blocks of cycles; each block typically begins with a baseline (on-peak zero) measurement before the analytical cycles. Adjust for samples with low signal or where higher precision is required.
Purpose: Multiple blocks per sample allow inspection of signal stability and within-measurement drift.

Description: Number of measurement cycles acquired per block. One cycle corresponds to a single set of simultaneous Faraday cup readings integrated for the duration specified in Integration Time per Cycle. Total integration time per sample = (Number of Cycles per Block) × (Integration Time per Cycle) × (Number of Blocks per Measurement).
Duration of signal integration per measurement cycle (seconds). Where different isotope channels use different integration schemes, record the time for each channel.
Purpose: Determines counting statistics per cycle. Longer integration times improve shot-noise precision but increase the impact of signal drift within the integration window. For high-gain (10¹² or 10¹³ Ω) amplifier channels, longer integration times are often required to accumulate sufficient charge.

Description: Method and timing for measuring the ion beam baseline (on-peak zero) during acquisition, and the portion of the acquisition it is taken from. Three approaches are in use: deflecting the ion beam (beam-off or electrostatic deflector); aspirating an acid blank; or collecting a defined number of laser-off cycles at the start of the same block. State which, and how many cycles or how long.
Purpose: The choice depends on how sample reaches the plasma — an acid blank applies only to solution introduction, and for laser ablation no blank can be aspirated mid-ablation.

Description: Method used to verify that every collector sits on a flat region of its peak top simultaneously, and the acceptance threshold applied before analysis begins. Typically assessed by scanning across the peak plateau, or by comparing ratios measured at slightly offset mass positions.
Purpose: Specific to simultaneous collection: a sequential instrument centres one mass at a time, whereas a multi-collector array must have all cups on flat peak tops at once or the measured ratio carries a peak-shape bias that no downstream correction removes.

Description: Peak flatness actually achieved in the session, assessed against the criterion registered by the procedure.
Purpose: Companion measured value to Peak Flatness Method and Threshold, following the criterion-versus-measurement split used for Oxide Production.

Description: Where the collision or reaction cell is supplied with a mixture of gases rather than a single gas, the identities and proportions of that mixture. Recorded separately from the gas identity. Record 'N/A' where a single gas is used.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'He:H2 92% : 8%' | 'N/A (single gas)' | 'None'
Purpose: The proportions change reaction efficiency and interference suppression independently of which gases are used.

Description: Where a monitored mass is produced by a reaction in the collision/reaction cell, the precursor ion, the reagent gas and the product ion measured. Records the mass-shift chemistry relating the mass measured to the analyte it reports, which the monitored mass alone does not state. Record 'N/A' where the analyte is measured on its own mass.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '125Te + 16O -> 141TeO+' | '77Se + 16O -> 93SeO+' | 'N/A (on-mass measurement)'

Description: Method used to determine the internal standard (IS) concentration for each unknown sample.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Single element from EPMA (SiO₂ wt% used as IS)' | 'Sum-of-major-oxide normalization to 100% (Liu et al. 2008)' | 'Stoichiometry-derived (Ca fixed at 10.1 wt% for calcite)' | 'No IS — external calibration only'
Purpose: Corrects for variable ablation yield between analyses.

Description: Element(s) used as the internal standard, the monitored isotope, and how the internal-standard concentration was established for unknowns. Where the element serves isotope-ratio work it must have a known isotopic composition and a mass close to the analyte's. Record 'None' together with the alternative used where no internal standard is applied.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '²⁹Si; SiO₂ wt% from EPMA' | '⁵³Cr; measured in preceding major-element run (run 1)' | 'None — sum of MgO+FeO+SiO₂+P₂O₅ = 100 wt% (Liu et al. 2008)' | For mapping procedures using oxide-sum normalization, report "None (oxide-sum normalization)" and cite the method reference.

Description: Approach used to convert measured ion signals to reported concentrations, and specifically any case where different analytes or analyte groups within one procedure are calibrated differently - different primary standards for different mass ranges or phases, or one element serving as internal standard while others are externally calibrated. Where a single strategy applies to all analytes, record that strategy. Where the procedure reports isotope ratios only and no concentrations, record 'Not applicable (isotope ratios only)'.
Example / Allowed Content: Single strategy: ⁴³Ca IS for all analytes (see Internal Standard fields); Multi-strategy: ⁴³Ca IS for major elements; NIST 610 external calibration for REEs; Fe+Ni+Co sum normalization for PGEs

Description: Method used to correct for laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF), including downhole fractionation during prolonged ablation, matrix-dependent fractionation between sample and calibration standard, and any specific correction algorithm applied. Reference the software function or publication.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Normalised to NIST SRM 612; no additional downhole correction' | 'Exponential downhole fractionation correction in Iolite using NIST SRM 612' | 'Linear time-drift correction applied per analysis'

Description: Strategy used to correct instrumental isotopic mass fractionation, also called mass bias or mass discrimination. Distinct from Elemental Fractionation Correction, which addresses inter-element fractionation during ablation and transport: this field addresses discrimination between isotopes of the same element, and applies wherever the procedure reports isotope ratios.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Standard-sample bracketing against NIST 612' | 'Co-aspirated Tl, exponential law' | 'None (elemental concentrations only)'

Description: The convention at which reported uncertainties are quoted — 1-sigma, 2-sigma, or a 95% confidence interval — and whether a measured spread is reported as a standard error or a standard deviation. State the convention applying to all values reported under this procedure, and state each separately where different reported quantities use different conventions. Distinct from Uncertainty Propagation Method, which addresses how component uncertainties are combined rather than how the result is quoted.
Example / Allowed Content: 2σ (95% confidence) | 1σ (68% confidence) | 95% confidence interval | 2 standard errors (2SE) | 1 standard deviation (1SD) | N/A | None
Purpose: A reported uncertainty is not interpretable without it: the same numeric value means different things at 1-sigma and at 95% confidence.

Description: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., Counting statistics only (1σ on integrated signal, Longerich et al. 1996) | SD of n replicate analyses used as combined uncertainty estimate | Full propagation: counting + calibration standard + IS uncertainty (specify formula)

Description: Whether an empirical correction was applied to account for systematic differences in laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF) patterns between the external calibration standard and the sample matrix.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Applied: 6.4% offset in Ca/Si determined by comparison with EPMA (Jenner & O'Neill 2012)' | 'Not applied; Ca used as IS to cancel LIEF offset' | 'Not applicable'

Description: Method used to define which portion of the acquired signal is integrated for each reported measurement, and the rule for excluding unstable or anomalous portions. State whether the interval is the full acquisition, a stable sub-interval selected by inspection, or selected by an automated criterion, and name the criterion.
Example / Allowed Content: Full acquisition | Stable interval selected by inspection | Automated threshold | Automated outlier rejection | Fixed time window | N/A | None

Description: The integration time actually used for the reported signal, in seconds - the time retained after the signal-integration interval has been applied, and therefore equal to or shorter than the total acquisition. Where the procedure computes it from an acquisition structure, record that basis.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 40 s | 60 s | Not applicable to mapping analysis: for mapping, the equivalent concept is the per-pixel cycle time, determined by the spectrometer dwell time settings.
Purpose: It is equal to or shorter than the Ablation Duration per Spot because the signal start and end transients are typically discarded.

Description: Criteria used to identify and exclude anomalous data - signal spikes, individual cycles, or whole replicate measurements - before the reported value is calculated. State where in the reduction sequence the filter is applied.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Significant single spikes visually identified and removed in Iolite' | 'Statistical filter: data points >3σ from running mean removed' | 'No filtering applied' | 'Automated spike detection in SILLS'

Description: Method used to subtract background and, where relevant, procedural blank from the measured signal. State what is subtracted - instrument background acquired with no sample reaching the plasma, an on-peak zero acquired on the same matrix, or a separately measured procedural blank - over what interval it is measured, and at what granularity it is applied.
Example / Allowed Content: Gas blank | On-peak zero | Solution blank | Procedural blank | On-peak zero + procedural blank | N/A | None

Description: Whether mathematical corrections for isobaric, polyatomic or residual interferences are applied in data reduction, supplementary to any suppression already achieved by chemical separation, mass resolution, or a collision/reaction cell. Detail for each affected mass is carried by Interfering Species and Interference Correction Method.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Yes — ⁸⁷Rb on ⁸⁷Sr, corrected from the ⁸⁵Rb monitor' | 'Yes — doubly-charged Er and Yb on the Sr and Rb masses' | 'No explicit corrections applied; medium resolution resolves the polyatomic interferences' | N/A | None

Description: The isobaric, polyatomic and doubly charged species that overlap the measured masses and are corrected in data reduction - direct isobars, oxides and argides, hydrides, and abundance-sensitivity tailing from an adjacent large beam. Name each species and the mass it affects.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '⁸⁷Rb on ⁸⁷Sr; ¹⁷⁰Yb²⁺ on ⁸⁵Rb' | '⁴⁰Ar³¹P⁺ on ⁷¹Ga; ⁴⁴Ca¹⁶O⁺ on ⁶⁰Ni' | '¹³⁷Ba¹⁶O⁺ on ¹⁵³Eu' | 'None'

Description: Equation or procedure used to calculate and remove each interference contribution, together with how its magnitude was established - a monitor mass measured simultaneously and scaled by natural abundance ratios, a production-rate factor measured on a reference material or interference standard solution, or a tailing factor measured on a pure standard. Name the reference material used.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Mathematical correction: ⁸⁷Sr_corrected = ⁸⁷Sr_measured − f(⁸⁷Rb/⁸⁵Rb) × ⁸⁵Rb' | 'Cool plasma (800 W) reduces ⁴⁰Ar-based argides by >90% for ⁶⁰Ni and ⁷¹Ga' | 'KED mode (He collision gas 4 ml min⁻¹) suppresses polyatomic interferences'

Description: Mass balance approach used to calculate sample mass fractions, and where applicable isotope ratios, from spike-sample isotope ratio measurements. For double-spike procedures the ratios and concentrations are co-determined through the spike inversion; for conventional isotope dilution the IUPAC ID equations are used. Record 'None' where neither isotope dilution nor double-spike methods are applied.
Example / Allowed Content: IUPAC isotope dilution equations | Double-spike inversion | None | N/A

Description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise carry-over of high-concentration or isotopically distinct material from a preceding measurement into the current one. Mitigation is applied primarily at measurement time, by allowing sufficient washout or rinse between successive introductions. At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Extended washout (≥60 s He flush) between high-concentration standards and unknowns' | 'Scan speed set so that washout time (<1 s) is shorter than pixel acquisition interval' | 'None required for this element suite'

Description: Post-acquisition normalization applied to the reported data beyond the primary calibration — for example correction to a reference value derived from secondary reference materials, or correction for a systematic bias those materials reveal. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'None' | '100% oxide sum normalization applied per pixel to enforce mass balance (Liu et al. 2008)' | 'Normalized to ⁸⁸Sr/⁸⁶Sr = 8.37521 for mass bias correction in Sr isotope analysis'

Description: An externally-calibrated factor that converts the measured quantity into the reported quantity, how it was determined, and its uncertainty. Applies where the conversion depends on a factor calibrated against a reference of independently known value, rather than on the instrument response alone. Distinct from the fields that name the calibration material and that state which approach applies to which analyte, where the technique has them: this field records the resulting factor itself.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., ID-TIMS: EARTHTIME ET535 or ET2535 tracer, calibrated per Condon et al. (2015) and McLean et al. (2015), with stated uncertainty | LA-ICP-MS: matrix-matched primary zircon RM of independently known age (91500, GJ-1, Plesovice) used for downhole-fractionation and Pb/U calibration, with the accepted age and its source

Description: The measured level of the analytical blank in the session, and — where the reported quantity is a ratio — its composition, since a blank subtracted from a ratio biases the result unless its own composition is known. Companion to the blank correction method.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Total procedural Pb blank 0.6 +/- 0.3 pg; blank Pb composition 206Pb/204Pb = 18.55, 207Pb/204Pb = 15.50, 208Pb/204Pb = 38.08 (long-term lab average, n = 42)' | 'Gas blank 120 counts/s at mass 206, subtracted per analysis'
Purpose: Follows the criterion-versus-measurement split the library applies wherever a procedure sets a threshold and an analysis reports a value against it.

Description: The rules determining which individual analyses contribute to a reported aggregate result, together with the outcome of applying them: how many analyses were acquired, how many were included, and on what grounds any were excluded. Distinct from within-analysis outlier filtering, which removes anomalous points inside a single analysis: this field decides which whole analyses enter the reported value.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '30 grains analysed, 24 included; excluded 4 discordant beyond -5% to +10% and 2 with Pb*/Pbc < 20' | 'All analyses included, no filter applied'
Purpose: Criteria and outcome are combined in one field because neither is interpretable without the other, following the precision/accuracy precedent.

Description: Mathematical law used to parameterize instrumental isotope mass fractionation as a function of mass difference. The linear law assumes fractionation proportional to mass difference. The power law is an alternative formulation. For double-spike procedures, the law is embedded in the inversion algorithm and must be consistent between spike calibration and sample data reduction.
Example / Allowed Content: Exponential | Linear | Power | N/A | None
Purpose: The exponential law (Maréchal et al. 1999) is most widely used and theoretically best justified for MC-ICP-MS.

Metadata Item: Internal Normalization Element and Isotope Ratio
Description: Element and isotope ratio used as the internal normalization standard for mass bias correction. Specify the element, the monitored isotope ratio (e.g., 113Cd/111Cd for Sb measurements), and the certified or consensus value used for correction. Record 'N/A' where the procedure does not use internal normalization.
Purpose: The measured ratio of the normalizing element is used to calculate the mass bias factor β using the chosen mass fractionation law, which is then applied to correct the analyte isotope ratios assuming β_norm ≈ β_analyte.

Description: The pair of enriched isotopes used to construct the double spike. Both isotopes must be naturally rare and free from isobaric interferences. The double spike composition must be accurately calibrated before use. Specify both isotope masses and the spike certificate or calibration reference. Record 'N/A' where the procedure does not use a double spike.
Purpose: The pair is chosen to minimise error magnification in the inversion.

Description: Target proportion of double-spike signal relative to total analyte signal in the spiked mixture, expressed as spike fraction (0–1) or spike:sample ratio. The optimum is analyte-system specific and is typically determined using the Double Spike Toolbox or equivalent. The achieved mixing ratio may deviate from the target within acceptable bounds (typically ±20% of optimal); the double-spike inversion corrects for actual mixing ratios. Record 'N/A' where the procedure does not use a double spike.
Purpose: An optimal mixing ratio minimises error propagation through the double-spike inversion.

Description: Mathematical algorithm used to simultaneously solve for the true sample isotope ratio and the mass fractionation factor from the measured spike-sample mixture. Common implementations: iterative Newton-Raphson solution, matrix algebraic approach, or published software (e.g., Rudge et al. 2009 Double Spike Toolbox). Specify the algorithm or software reference and version. Record 'N/A' where the procedure does not use a double spike.

The equation used to convert the measured quantities into an age or date, together with a citation for that equation. Name the equation unambiguously; where a procedure supports more than one, state which is used and under what conditions. Distinct from Age Model and Software, which records how multiple analyses are combined into a single reported result.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 206Pb/238U and 207Pb/235U date equations (Jaffey et al. 1971 decay constants) | 207Pb/206Pb date | Wetherill concordia intercept | Tera-Wasserburg concordia intercept | 238U/206Pb-207Pb/206Pb isochron
Purpose: Required by every geochronology reporting standard surveyed (Condon et al. 2024; Schaen et al. 2021; Rooney et al. 2024; Flowers et al. 2024; Kohn et al. 2024; Mahan et al. 2023).

Description: The kind of date or age the procedure reports. Where more than one type is reported, list all, separated by semicolons.
Example / Allowed Content: Weighted mean 206Pb/238U | Weighted mean 207Pb/235U | Weighted mean 207Pb/206Pb | Concordia upper intercept | Concordia lower intercept | Tera-Wasserburg intercept | Single-grain date | Isochron date | N/A | None
Purpose: Most dating systems derive several different date types from the same measurements, so a reported age is ambiguous without this. Kohn et al. (2024) carry this as a named required item ("fission-track age type"); the equivalent distinction is required by all five other standards surveyed.

Description: How any non-radiogenic, inherited or pre-existing component of the measured signal was accounted for, including the composition assumed, its source, and its uncertainty. Record 'None' where the measured quantity accumulates from zero and no such component exists.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., Stacey & Kramers (1975) two-stage model Pb at the interpreted age | 204Pb-based correction | 207Pb-based correction | 208Pb-based correction | Tera-Wasserburg anchored lower intercept | measured Pb from co-genetic K-feldspar | None (Pb*/Pbc sufficiently high that correction is negligible; state the threshold)
Purpose: Applies to five of the six dating systems surveyed; fission track is the sole genuine exception, as tracks accumulate from zero. The value actually applied is frequently sample-specific (a two-stage model composition evaluated at the interpreted age) or session-derived (a trapped composition solved from an isochron intercept), so a revision to the assumed composition should not require registering a new procedure. Same reasoning as Rule 5's Constants and Reference Values Used.

Description: The proportion of the measured signal that is radiogenic, as opposed to inherited, initial or otherwise non-radiogenic. Measured companion to Inherited or Initial Signal Correction.
Example / Allowed Content: Reported for U-Pb as Pb*/Pbc, the ratio of radiogenic to common Pb. e.g., '1250' | '18' | 'range 12-340 across 24 analyses'
Purpose: It indicates how strongly the reported age depends on the assumed non-radiogenic composition — a result derived from a low radiogenic fraction is sensitive to that assumption in a way a high-fraction result is not, and that sensitivity is invisible from the age and its uncertainty alone. Follows the criterion-versus-measurement split used for Oxide Production.

Description: The statistical model used to combine individual analyses into a single reported age, including any criteria governing which model is applied. Record the model only — the software implementing it belongs in Data Reduction Software (Group 3), whose scope already extends to age calculation; where reduction and age regression use different packages, list both there.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., Weighted mean with MSWD-based uncertainty expansion | York (1969) regression | IsoplotR Model-1, escalating to Model-3 where MSWD exceeds the stated cutoff | Bayesian / Monte Carlo age model
Purpose: This is a methodological choice that changes the result: a Model-1 and a Model-3 regression of the same data yield different ages and different uncertainties. Required in some form by all six geochronology reporting standards surveyed.

Description: The zero point from which the reported age is measured, where this is not the present day, and the date it corresponds to. Record 'Present day' where the conventional datum applies. Where the datum is not the present, record it explicitly: year of sample collection for luminescence, end of irradiation for 40Ar/39Ar decay corrections.
Example / Allowed Content: Present day (the conventional datum for U-Pb; state explicitly rather than leaving blank)
Purpose: Required in these cases by Mahan et al. (2023) and Schaen et al. (2021).

Description: Correction for initial disequilibrium in intermediate daughter products of the U decay chains — principally 230Th, and where relevant 231Pa — together with the Th/U or Pa/U partitioning value assumed and its source. Record 'None' with a justification where no correction was applied.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '230Th correction applied, Th/U(magma) = 2.8 assumed from whole-rock' | '230Th and 231Pa corrections applied (Crowley et al. 2007)' | 'None (sample older than 100 Ma; effect below stated uncertainty)'
Purpose: Unique to U-Pb among dating systems, because the chains are long enough for intermediate-daughter disequilibrium at crystallisation to bias the 206Pb/238U date, most severely in young samples. Condon et al. (2024) write "we recommend these dates be reported corrected for initial 230Th and 231Pa daughter isotope disequilibrium" — recommended rather than required.

Description: How discordance between the 206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U and 207Pb/206Pb chronometers is defined for this procedure, and the discordance values obtained. State the formula used. The rule for excluding discordant analyses, and how many were excluded, belong in Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteria.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '100 x (1 - [206Pb/238U date] / [207Pb/206Pb date])' | '2-sigma concordia ellipse overlap' | 'discordance -3% to +7% across 24 analyses'
Purpose: Genuinely specific to U-Pb: it is the only system in routine use with two independent decay schemes in the same mineral, so agreement between them is an internal consistency test no other system can run. Condon et al. (2024) write that for samples older than a few hundred million years "it is also useful to provide a measure of discordance" — useful and age-conditional rather than required. Several definitions are in circulation and they are not interchangeable.

Description: The correlation coefficient between pairs of reported quantities whose uncertainties are not independent, together with the pair it applies to and how it was obtained.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'rho(206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U) = 0.83, from the data reduction software error propagation' | 'rho = 0.31 (double-spike inversion covariance)'
Purpose: Concordia and isochron regressions cannot be reconstructed without it.

Description: Physical constants and reference values used in data reduction to calculate the final reported quantity (e.g., decay constants for age calculation, standard isotope ratios, or other citable reference values used in a correction or calculation), together with their source. Distinct from the Group 6 reference-material fields, which document accepted values for specific calibration/validation materials rather than universal physical constants. Record "None" if no citable, revisable physical constants feed into this procedure's data reduction.

Name and reference material identifier of the primary reference material(s) against which the instrument is calibrated — converting raw signal intensities to concentrations, or anchoring an isotope ratio as the bracketing standard or zero-delta reference. Give the material name, its source or supplier, and a citation for the accepted values used. Where calibration instead uses the vendor's stored library or theoretical response factors rather than measured reference materials — 'standardless' or 'semi-quantitative' quantification — record that here, naming the library or model used. 'None' means no calibration was performed at all, which is a different answer.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'NIST SRM 612 (Jochum et al. 2011, doi:10.1111/j.1751-908X.2011.00120.x)' | 'USGS BCR-2G (GeoReM preferred values, georem.mpch-mainz.gwdg.de)'
Purpose: Results calibrated against different published values for the same material are not directly comparable.

Description: How often the primary calibration or bracketing standard is measured relative to unknown samples within a session. Specify the bracketing scheme where a fixed one is used, such as one standard measurement before and after each sample.
Example / Allowed Content: Before and after every 5 unknowns | Bracketing every 10 samples | Start and end of session only | N/A | None
Purpose: For LA-ICP-MS, this defines the bracketing interval between calibration standard ablations used to monitor and correct for instrumental drift.

Description: Quality-control reference material(s) measured as unknowns alongside samples to assess accuracy independently and to monitor drift. Give the material name, its source, and a citation for the accepted or reference values used for comparison.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'NIST SRM 610 (Jochum et al. 2011); GOR132-G (Jochum et al. 2006)' | 'BHVO-2G (GeoReM), BCR-2G (GeoReM)'

Description: Detection limit, one per reported concentration variable (one per analyte, these being the same set). State the units and whether the values are procedure-typical estimates or session-specific measured values. The calculation method is recorded separately in Detection Limit Method. Record 'N/A' where the procedure reports no concentrations.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '0.003 ng g⁻¹ (La), 0.005 ng g⁻¹ (Ce) (3σ background; Longerich et al. 1996)' | 'Range: 0.005–23.5 µg g⁻¹ across all measured isotopes (Pettke et al. 2012)'

Description: Formula or approach used to calculate the detection limits, with a citation for the method where one exists. Must be consistent with the values reported in Detection Limit.
Example / Allowed Content: 3σ blank | 3σ background | 3σ counting statistics | 3× blank mean | Poisson statistics | N/A | None

Description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the limit of quantification (LOQ): the lowest concentration reliably measurable with acceptable precision and accuracy. Required when concentrations near the LOD are reported.
Example / Allowed Content: 10σ blank | 10σ background | 10× LOD | 3.3× LOD | S/N ≥ 10 | N/A | None
Purpose: Concentrations between LOD and LOQ are detectable but not reliably quantifiable.

Description: Uncertainty predicted from counting statistics — the theoretical limit set by the Poisson distribution of the counts accumulated — for each reported quantity per analysis, with the sigma level stated. Derived from the counts on the analyte together with those on any background or blank subtracted from it. Distinct from the scatter actually observed within a measurement or between repeated measurements, which is recorded separately.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '2SE predicted from counting statistics over 45 cycles' | '~0.6% (1 sigma), counting statistics plus propagated uncertainties' | 'N/A'
Keyed By: sample > sampling unit x reported property
Purpose: Where a procedure reports both, agreement indicates the measurement is shot-noise limited, and a larger observed scatter indicates a further source of variance.

Metadata Item: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Precision of a single measurement, derived from the scatter of the cycles, sweeps or integrations that make it up, together with the method used to assess it. State the statistic (2SE, 2SD, 1s RSD), the number of cycles it is computed over, and the reported quantity it applies to. Distinct from Counting Statistics Error, which records the uncertainty predicted from the counts rather than the scatter observed; where a procedure reports both, record the observed value here and the predicted value there.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '2SE = 2SD/sqrt(n), n = 45 cycles' | '+/-0.001-0.002 (2SE) on 206Pb/204Pb' | '~2.6% (2SE) on single-spot ages' | 'N/A'
Keyed By: sample > sampling unit x reported property
Purpose: This is the finest of the three precision levels the library records, below within-session and between-session precision: it describes the repeatability of one analysis rather than agreement between analyses, and is normally the smallest of the three.

Metadata Item: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Precision of repeated measurements within a single analytical session and the method used to assess it. Report both the assessment method and the precision values. The assessment method must specify the reference material or standard measured, the number of replicates n, and the statistic reported (1s RSD, 2s RSD, 2SD, 2SE, 95% CI). Distinct from the internal precision of a single measurement, which derives from counting statistics over the cycles of that measurement rather than from repeated analyses.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '1σ RSD = 1.5% for Ba, 2.3% for La (n=5 on NIST SRM 612 per session)' | 'Mapping: 4% 1σ RSD across 3 GRM map areas at session start and end (n=3)'

Metadata Item: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Precision of measurements across multiple analytical sessions over weeks to months — long-term or intermediate precision — and the method used to assess it. Report both the assessment method and the precision values, specifying the reference material, the number of measurements and sessions, the time span covered, and the statistic reported.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '2σ RSD = 3% for Eu/Eu* on GOR132-G across 12 sessions over 8 months' | '1σ RSD = 2% for most REEs on BHVO-2G across 17 sessions over 3 years (n=85 analyses)'
Purpose: Long-term precision is normally poorer than within-session precision and is the figure a data user should carry when comparing results from different sessions.

Description: Offset between measured and accepted values for secondary reference materials, and the method used to assess it. Specify the reference material and the source of its accepted values, the number of analyses, and the quantities assessed. Report systematic biases and their likely causes. Express the offset in the form appropriate to what the procedure reports - percent relative bias for concentrations, or deviation in delta or ratio units for isotopic quantities.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Within ±5% of GeoReM preferred values for most REEs on GOR132-G (n=15); +8% for Nb (known matrix sensitivity)' | '±3% for all elements on BHVO-2G vs. GeoReM (n=20)'

Description: The statistic reported to show whether scatter among the contributing analyses exceeds what analytical uncertainty alone predicts, together with its value. The procedure may still state an acceptance threshold, which belongs with the inclusion criteria.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'MSWD = 1.13 (n = 24), probability of fit 0.31' | 'MSWD = 4.2; excess scatter attributed to protracted crystallisation, Model-3 regression applied'
Purpose: Answers whether a reported aggregate is defensible as a single population. The value cannot be known before the analysis.

Description: Any procedure- or analysis-specific information not captured by a structured field anywhere in this TAPP — including anomalies, deviations from the registered procedure, instrument modifications, and supplementary context. Scope is the whole document, not Group 6: this is the last field of the TAPP and covers all six groups. Use sparingly; a structured field is preferred for anything that can be formally categorised.
